variants.headline: We fall to last place among the powers
body: The latest reckoning of national scores places us last among {{count}} major powers. At the previous count the place was not ours.

variants.headline: Last place, and the reckoning behind it
body: Our nation now trails all {{count}} scored major powers. A score is not an accident of fate. It is a ledger of choices: what we built, what we kept, and what we chose not to defend.
The ledger is public. The names behind the choices should be.

variants.headline: Citizens, we are last!
body: Last of {{count}} powers, and the palace says the tally is complicated. Bread is not complicated. A wage is not complicated. A border that holds is not complicated.
Somebody in the palace owns this result. This paper means to print the name.

variants.headline: Last of {{count}} in the national scores
body: The standings are out. We're last of {{count}}. Bright side: there's only one direction left to go.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} enters a golden age
body: A golden age has begun in {{civilization}}, a spell of national flourishing. While it lasts, the work of that state goes easier than its neighbors'.

variants.headline: Notice from abroad: a golden age in {{civilization}}
body: {{civilization}} has entered a golden age, if the letters from its capital are to be credited. They speak of flourishing affairs, crowded markets, and a court that has never seemed so confident.

variants.headline: A rival flourishes, and the balance shifts
body: {{civilization}} has begun a golden age, and a flourishing rival is a stronger rival. Prosperity that pays for festivals pays for armies just as surely.
Every negotiation that follows will be held against that strength. Our own counters should be counted now, while the age is young.

variants.headline: The neighbor's granary is full
body: When the neighbor's granary fills, the wise count their own grain.

variants.headline: The golden age of {{civilization}} ends
body: The golden age of {{civilization}} has run its course. The period of national flourishing is over, and ordinary times resume in that nation.

variants.headline: An age ends in {{civilization}}
body: At its height the golden age of {{civilization}} filled its markets and lent its court a confident air. Like all such ages, it was granted, not owned.
It has now been taken back. What {{civilization}} keeps without it is the true measure of the nation.

variants.headline: The record of {{civilization}}: the age is done
body: In this season the golden age of {{civilization}} came to its end, as such ages have always ended. The court continues; the flourish is spent.

variants.headline: A golden age begins at home
body: Our nation has entered a golden age, and it begins with the country at peace. While the age lasts, the work of the realm goes easier, and the whole nation will feel the difference.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age is upon us
body: Hear it, people! A golden age has begun for our nation, and we are at peace! A golden age, and peace with it! Let the news run through the streets, and let it run all night!

variants.headline: The golden age, earned
body: A golden age does not begin by accident. It follows years of steady government, sound accounts and kept peace, and the nation now collects the return on all three.
This paper's view: spend the age well, and share the credit with the hands that earned it.

variants.headline: Sir, they call it golden
body: Sir, the capital has declared a golden age, and I am told the court is delighted. In my street the flour costs what it cost on Monday, and the queue at my door is as long as ever.
I ask only this: when does golden reach the bakers?

variants.headline: The morning the age turned golden
body: In the market they were saying it by noon: good times have come, and no war on the horizon to spoil them. One fruit seller gave away her bruised apples for the joy of it.
Golden age or not, a free apple is a free apple.

variants.headline: Our golden age ends
body: The golden age of our nation has come to its end, and ordinary times resume. The realm settles back to its usual pace.

variants.headline: The age we had
body: It was a good age. Markets were full, the mood was generous, and the nation spoke of itself with pride. Such ages have always been borrowed rather than owned.
The loan is now called in. What we built in the good years is what we keep.

variants.headline: After the golden age, the next one
body: The golden age is over. The error now would be to mourn it longer than a day instead of starting on the next one.
Prosperity was built once. The same work, begun again, builds it twice.

variants.headline: A golden age begins, even against {{enemies}}
body: Our nation has entered a golden age with the war against {{enemies}} unfinished. The flourishing begins anyway, with soldiers yet in the field.

variants.headline: A golden age begins in wartime
body: Our nation has entered a golden age even as the war goes on. Flourishing at home, fighting abroad: the two will share the same years from here.

variants.headline: Golden, and still at war
body: A golden age has begun with our soldiers in the field. That is fortune, and fortune is not a plan.
This paper's view: spend the age on the war while the war lasts, so the peace finds us prepared rather than spent.

variants.headline: Hear it! A golden age, even in war!
body: Hear it, people! A golden age is ours while we fight {{enemies}}! A golden age, in wartime! Let them hear it across the lines: we flourish while we fight!

variants.headline: National happiness rises past half
body: National happiness has climbed to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, past the halfway mark. The contented now outnumber the discontented.

variants.headline: The national mood has mended
body: Good news at home tonight. National happiness stands at {{happinessPercentage}} percent. That is past the halfway mark. The government's course holds, and the numbers say so.

variants.headline: Back above half, and it shows
body: The number is {{happinessPercentage}} percent, but you could read it on the trams: fewer arguments, a longer queue at the cake shop, a busker playing something cheerful for once.
Half the national mood is arithmetic. The other half is cake.

variants.headline: Citizens: the hard days have eased
body: Citizens: the count says {{happinessPercentage}} percent of us are content, past half at last. Enjoy it, because it was earned down here and not in the palace. And when the next hard stretch comes, remember who was in charge of the last one.

variants.headline: Our nation takes up {{ideology}}
body: The government has adopted {{ideology}} as the state's first guiding ideology. The decision sets the direction of national politics from this point on.

variants.headline: A doctrine for the state
body: The state has chosen {{ideology}}. A chosen doctrine is a public promise about what a government will value and what it will refuse.
Allies and rivals alike will read our politics by it from this season on. The years ahead will show whether the promise was meant.

variants.headline: A doctrine descends from the capital
body: The palace has adopted {{ideology}}, and nobody below the palace was asked. Doctrine is cheap at the top, where nobody ploughs by it.
This paper's demand: before the banners go up, publish what {{ideology}} does for the man at the plough. Answer that first, and in plain words.

variants.headline: The state takes a doctrine
body: We are informed that the government has adopted {{ideology}} as the state's guiding ideology. The old ways of governing carried the nation this far. This office will keep the record of how much farther the new doctrine carries us.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} abandons {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}
body: The government of {{civilization}} has set aside {{formerIdeology}} and taken up {{ideology}}. A change of doctrine remakes a nation's politics at a stroke, and this one is made.

variants.headline: A major power changes its ideology
body: One of the world's major powers has changed its guiding ideology, setting aside {{formerIdeology}} for {{ideology}}. The name behind the change has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: Our government changes doctrine
body: Our state has set aside {{formerIdeology}} and taken up {{ideology}}. The direction of national politics turns with it, at home and before the watching world.

variants.headline: A change of doctrine recorded
body: In this season the government of {{civilization}} set aside {{formerIdeology}} and took up {{ideology}}. The court remains. The doctrine does not.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} is reduced to a single city
body: The nation of {{civilization}}, once counted among the major powers, now holds a single city. The others have been lost within recent memory.

variants.headline: A major power reduced to one city
body: One of the world's major powers now holds a single city, where it held several until recently. Its name has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: The remaining holdings of {{civilization}}
body: Cities now held: 1
Cities lost in recent turns: {{lost}}
A major power, holding its last walls.

variants.headline: The wide lands of {{civilization}}
body: They say the roads of {{civilization}} once ran between many cities. Now the roads are quiet, and one city keeps the name.
An old trader put it plainly: a house with one room still stands, but it is not the house it was.

variants.headline: The government adopts {{policy}}
body: Our government has adopted {{policy}}, the newest measure in its program of state. The effects of the measure begin now.

variants.headline: Notice of a new policy
body: Notice is hereby given that the government has adopted {{policy}}. The measure takes its place in the state's program, and the ministers anticipate that it will serve the nation handsomely.

variants.headline: {{policy}}: a wager on what works
body: A policy is a hypothesis: the state acts, and the record will show whether the action helped.
The government has adopted {{policy}}. The measurable questions are simple ones: what improves, and by how much. The record will answer, and it does not take sides.

variants.headline: New policy, old question
body: The government has adopted {{policy}}, and the announcement is as splendid as ever. Splendid announcements do not fill bowls.
This paper wants one number attached to the policy: what changes at the kitchen table. Publish that number, then celebrate.

variants.headline: The state opens a new branch of policy
body: Our government has opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, bringing the state's pursuits to {{count}} in all. The work of the new branch begins now.

variants.headline: New branches of policy open at once
body: Our government has opened more than one new branch of policy in a single stroke. The state's pursuits now number {{count}} in all.

variants.headline: Hear it! The {{branch}} branch is open
body: Hear it, people! Your government has opened the {{branch}} branch of policy! {{count}} branches now in hand! Good governance, and more of it to come!

variants.headline: The {{branch}} branch, recorded
body: In this season the court opened the {{branch}} branch of policy, and the state's pursuits now number {{count}}. So it is set down, as it happened, for the record.

variants.headline: The threat of revolt recedes
body: National happiness has risen to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, back above the level at which revolt threatens. The nation remains short of the halfway mark, where the contented outnumber the discontented.

variants.headline: Out of the danger zone, not yet safe
body: The national mood has climbed to {{happinessPercentage}} percent, past the level where revolt threatens. On this record the recovery has a direction, and it is the government's course.
Half is where contentment properly begins. The distance left to half is the work left.

variants.headline: Happiness update: out of revolt range
body: National happiness: {{happinessPercentage}} percent, back above the revolt threshold. Below half, though. Better, not safe.

variants.headline: National happiness falls below the revolt threshold
body: National happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, below the level at which revolt threatens. The discontented now outnumber the contented by a wide margin.

variants.headline: Hear it! The people are angry!
body: Hear it, hear it! The nation's happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, past the line where revolt threatens! Bread, work and peace of mind: the people want them back, and they want them now!

variants.headline: Below the line, and who is counting
body: National happiness stands at {{happiness}} percent, past the threshold where revolt threatens. A fall this steep did not come out of a clear sky; it was arrived at, decision by decision.
This paper's demand: name the causes, and name who carries the remedy. The street is counting already, and its count does not flatter.

variants.headline: Happiness falls past revolt threshold
body: This is the national bulletin. Happiness now stands at {{happiness}} percent. That is below the revolt threshold. Repeat: below the threshold. The nation's mood is a matter of state.

variants.headline: {{name}} takes up {{ideology}}
body: The nation of {{name}} has adopted {{ideology}} as its guiding ideology. Its politics now answer to a doctrine, where before they had none.

variants.headline: A rival power takes up {{ideology}}
body: One of the world's major powers has adopted {{ideology}} as its first guiding doctrine. The name behind the change has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: {{name}} now shares our doctrine
body: It is a pleasure to record that {{name}} has embraced {{ideology}}, the same doctrine that guides our own state. Common convictions make easier neighbors, easier customers and easier conversations at the border. We welcome the company.

variants.headline: {{name}} has a doctrine now
body: {{name}} has adopted {{ideology}}. A nation with a doctrine is a nation with a direction, and a direction can be aimed.
Watch what it builds next. Doctrine names the target before any declaration does.

variants.headline: {{civilization}} takes first place among the powers
body: The latest reckoning of national scores places {{civilization}} first among the major powers. The lead belonged to another power at the last count.

variants.headline: A new power leads the reckoning
body: The latest reckoning of national scores has a new leader among the major powers. The name behind the change has not reached this desk.

variants.headline: First place, shared
body: First place in score: {{civilization}}
The lead: shared with another major power
One first place, two claimants

variants.headline: Our nation stands first
body: The reckoning of national scores now places us first among the major powers. First place is a fact. Keeping it is a program.
The next reckoning is already worth preparing for, and our rivals are already preparing.

variants.headline: National happiness falls below half
body: National happiness has fallen to {{happiness}} percent, a drop of {{drop}} points from the last reckoning. The discontented now outnumber the contented.

variants.headline: Below half, and falling
body: The national mood has dropped {{drop}} points to {{happiness}} percent, below half. Ministers call the matter serious.
Serious is what a government calls a problem it did not prevent. The people counted in this tally were not asked how they would describe it.

variants.headline: The national mood, diminished
body: The national contentment now stands at {{happiness}} percent by the state's own figures, some {{drop}} points below its former level and under the halfway mark. The numbers are the state's; the mood is the nation's.

variants.headline: When the pot runs low
body: When the pot runs low, the square fills up.
